claim: Maximum softmax probability (MSP) is the standard baseline for flagging both misclassified and out-of-distribution inputs, because correct predictions tend to have higher max softmax, but the authors note it can be beaten.
evidence: "Correctly classified examples tend to have greater maximum softmax probabilities"; "the baseline can sometimes be surpassed" (Hendrycks & Gimpel, arXiv:1610.02136)

claim: The energy score (logsumexp of logits) is a drop-in post-hoc replacement for softmax confidence that reduces average FPR@TPR95 by 18.03% on a CIFAR-10 WideResNet.
evidence: "using the energy score reduces the average FPR (at TPR 95%) by 18.03% compared to the softmax confidence score"; softmax methods "suffer from overconfident posterior distributions for OOD data" (Liu et al., arXiv:2010.03759)

claim: Misclassification detection and OOD detection need different scores: OOD detectors evaluated for selective classification with OOD data rank differently and generally fail to beat the softmax baseline.
evidence: "existing post-hoc methods perform quite differently compared to when evaluated only on OOD detection"; SIRC "is able to consistently match or outperform the baseline for SCOD" while existing OOD methods "fail to do so" (Xia & Bouganis, arXiv:2207.07506)

claim: On a fine-grained 8-disease strawberry dataset, open-set methods with outlier exposure detect unknown diseases with AUROC about 0.97, while OpenMax without outlier exposure reached only 70.1% accuracy.
evidence: Two-head network AUROC 0.972, unknown recall 94.9%; OpenMatch AUROC 0.971; "assuming outlier exposure during training is helpful for detecting unknown diseases"; "The outlier exposure provided a significant 16.4% increase in accuracy" (Frontiers in Plant Science 2022)

claim: Across five public plant-disease datasets, max-logit OOD scoring on a visual-prompt-tuned pretrained model reaches AUROC 94.8% with only 8 shots per class, close to 95.2% with full fine-tuning on all data.
evidence: "the max-logit-based on visual prompt tuning achieves an AUROC score of 94.8% in the 8-shot setting" vs 95.2% full fine-tuning (Dong et al., Scientific Reports 14:17900, 2024)
